main_text.p: Syriacæ ab ipso conscriptæ hæc, אבון קרישא ܡܠܟ ܝܕܥܬܢܐ ܡܪܝ ܢܝܢܘܪܝܘܣ ܒܦܪܝܢܝܐ ܪܡܬܘܐ ܐܒܘ ܐܠܦܪܢܓ ܒܪ ܐܗܪܘܢ ܐܣܝܐ ܡܘܠܝܛܝܢܝܐ Pater noster Sanctus, rex doctorum, Mor Gregorius, Doctor Orientis, qui idem est Abul Pharaj, filius Ahronis medici Militiniensis, i.e. Malatiensis. Ipsi igitur nomen proprium, Gregorius, agnomen à filio desumptum, Abul-Pharaj, à patre, Ebn Ahrun, titulo quasi proprio, omnium consensu ملك العلما doctorum rex insignitur. Eruditione autem sibi famam conciliasse, non solùm apud Christianos, sed & apud Iudæos & Mohammeditas videtur. Utrorúmq; manibus tritam historiam ejus, testatur duorum quibus usus sum, exemplarium alterum, cujus margines ipsorum notis passim interpolati, & ad cujus calcem, de autore censura hæc docti alicujus Mohammedani adscribitur, مصنفه ابو الفرج بن حكيما كان كثير الاطلاع وحصل علوما شتى واتقنها وانفرد بالطب في زمانه حتى شدت اليه الرحال بارض المغرب كان عيسويا واخذ عنه كثير من فضلا المسلمين وقيل انه عاش بعد موته رجع

page.notes: The Syriac/Hebrew-looking letters in the first line and the Syriac-looking line after it are hard to read at this resolution; they are transcribed as best seen and should be checked against the scan. The Arabic lines are also uncertain: the opening word of the first Arabic line and the exact forms in the last lines may be wrong. Marked as read but not verified letter by letter. The Arabic word after "ملك العلما" appears to be cut short in the scan; it is copied as seen. Some Arabic and the initial Hebrew-script line may need [?] markers on inspection.
